name: Consumer virtual reality
title: Why early VR failed, and when consumer VR became viable
question: Why did early virtual reality fail, and when did consumer VR become viable?
answer: VPL Research (1984), Jaron Lanier's company, sold the first commercial VR gloves and headsets; it went bankrupt in 1990 and its patents were later bought by Sun Microsystems. Rendering and displays cost tens of thousands of dollars. Oculus (2012) built a headset from phone-grade displays and gaming GPUs; Facebook bought it for about $2B in 2014.
verdict_reason: Phone displays and consumer GPUs made a few-hundred-dollar headset possible in 2012.

constraint.name: GPU and display cost
constraint.detail: Convincing VR needs high-resolution displays and fast rendering; both cost workstation money until smartphones and gaming GPUs.

crossing.text: Phone-panel displays and consumer GPUs make the Oculus Rift prototype possible.
